notes: Guided launch interview question bank (doc 03). One focused question per turn; at most three short choices including the client's own answer. Conditions are evaluated against the answer ledger; a question whose condition fails is skipped, never asked. Field states: provided | verified_existing | recommended_unapproved | approved_recommendation | unknown | not_applicable. Blank is not not_applicable.

choices: Choose a setup for me to review
questions.prompt: How would you like to set this up?
questions.reason: Chooses how much the interview recommends vs asks.

questions.prompt: What are you offering, and who is it for? A rough sentence, a link, or pasted notes are all fine.
questions.reason: The main offer and its buyer anchor every later choice.

questions.prompt: What should be different for someone after they use it?
questions.reason: The realistic result the launch promises; never an invented guarantee.

questions.prompt: What are the three biggest problems it solves for them? Short phrases are fine.
questions.reason: The owner's method builds the page from three distinct pains.

questions.prompt: What does the buyer actually get? A rough list is fine - include amounts, access time, or dates where you know them.
questions.reason: Deliverables and exclusions are commercial facts the buyer relies on.

questions.prompt: Do you have any real results, stories, or kind words from buyers we may use? Paste or link them, or say none yet.
questions.reason: Proof must be real and attributed; missing proof is never invented.
questions.recommendation_rule: When none is supplied, mark proof not_applicable and plan a proof-free narrative; never fabricate testimonials.

questions.prompt: Will buyers choose one offer, or choose between a few packages?
questions.reason: Decides whether a product selection page exists in the route.
questions.recommendation_rule: Two or more meaningfully different main packages described in Phase A -> recommend multiple_options; one offer -> single_simple. Different payment schedules alone do not require a selection page.

choices: Suggest one for me to review
questions.prompt: Do you already have a price for it, or should I suggest a starting price for you to review?
questions.reason: A price is a commercial fact; a suggestion is a proposal, never a proven optimum.
questions.recommendation_rule: A suggested price must state its rationale from known delivery cost, scope and supplied market context, and stays recommended_unapproved until the plan is approved. Unknown price is recorded unknown - never zero.

questions.prompt: How do buyers pay - all at once, monthly, in parts, or a trial first?
questions.reason: Billing shape changes the checkout and the schedule the buyer must see.

questions.prompt: Would a small extra item help them use what they are buying? It can appear as an optional add-on before they pay.
questions.reason: The bump is an optional component on checkout, default unchecked.
questions.recommendation_rule: Recommend a bump only when a small, distinct add-on is named in supplied facts and its entitlements are not already included in the main offer.

questions.prompt: After they buy, is there a useful upgrade or extra product you want to offer?
questions.reason: Upsell 1 must add incremental value, never repeat the purchase.
questions.recommendation_rule: Recommend U1 only from a distinct second product in supplied facts; name the assumption and confirm it is actually deliverable.

questions.prompt: If they pass on that upgrade, is there a smaller version or an easier way to buy it?
questions.reason: The downsell is a changed scope or changed terms - a lower installment is not a lower total price.
questions.recommendation_rule: If no good alternative exists in supplied facts, recommend no downsell rather than inventing one.

questions.prompt: After someone takes the upgrade or the smaller offer, should we offer one more helpful product? It is the same page reached from either one.
questions.reason: Upsell 2 is one canonical page with dependencies on U1 or D1.
questions.recommendation_rule: Recommend U2 only from a distinct third product in supplied facts that does not duplicate the bump or a package inclusion.

questions.prompt: Do we already have your logo, colors, and a real photo of you saved? If something is missing, you can add it through the secure upload - please do not paste passwords or private files here.
questions.reason: Real brand assets are reused, never synthetically substituted.

questions.prompt: Should the main page be the standard length, or the long, detailed version?
questions.reason: Copy profile is a recorded client choice that shapes the landing page request.
questions.recommendation_rule: Recommend from supplied offer complexity and audience reading needs, labeled as a recommendation.

questions.prompt: Should this go into your existing Convert & Flow account?
questions.reason: Account and location IDs come from verified access (S06), never from recitation.

questions.prompt: Use your connected image service, or would you like a recommendation?
questions.reason: The provider is named only after availability is checked; a subscription is not proof of API access.

choices: Yes, I will give a limit
questions.prompt: Is there a spending limit for making the pictures and other paid pieces? Paid work needs its own OK, separate from approving the plan.
questions.reason: Paid-generation budget is a separate scoped approval (paid_asset_budget), not implied by plan approval.

questions.prompt: Here is the launch I recommend. Do you approve this plan for building, or would you like a change?
questions.reason: Approval binds to the exact plan hash and revision; recommendation mode never approves by itself.
